# Summary

Example University holds its collection records in three systems that disagree. This proposal describes a four-week engagement that produces one working view across all three, built with your staff and documented so they can maintain it.

# The problem

Three systems hold overlapping records: the ILS, the digital repository and a spreadsheet kept by Special Collections. Each is right about something. None is right about everything.

## What we heard

In twelve conversations across four departments, the same request came up: show me the conflicts, side by side, before I decide.

# The method

We work in four movements, always in this order.

1. **Listen.** Sit with the people who use each system and write down what they actually do.
2. **Trace.** Follow every record type to the system that last wrote it.
3. **Tune.** Build one working prototype that reads from all three.
4. **Echo.** Hand it over with documentation your staff can keep.

# Deliverables and schedule

| Week | Movement | Deliverable |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Listen | Written record of current workflows |
| 2 | Trace | Record lineage for each system |
| 3 | Tune | Working prototype, first review |
| 4 | Echo | Handover, documentation, second review |

# What you get

A prototype that runs on your infrastructure, source code with a plain README, and two review sessions with the cataloging team.
